After the dotted/accented final vowel the low terminal s follows directly; there is no additional e body before it.

The long p descender, the n/c/t run, tall t and uels ending support ponctuels. The low run before p does not expose two separate o bodies, and a raised tick can be an i dot; mono versus uni remains open. Neither reading gives marqués.
Pour, the second p descender and pouvoir, followed by the reconstitu- sequence with two tall t strokes, lie on the ordinary baseline before bel et bien; this is not the interlinear insertion.

changes.place: Opening: live article before the cancellation
changes.ink: The live article has a looped l followed by a low e/s run; its last stroke is not the a in H. The article is outside the cancellation, and the following singular commutation is retained literally.

The beginning under the strike has the low c/o/v-like sequence and a raised mid-word tick compatible with covariances. The heavy horizontal strike conceals several bodies, so the tentative reading remains doubtful; connaissance is not adopted.
The underline ends under the word and the gap before Déterminer has no separate full stop. The emph/underline macro distinction itself is not counted.
Two high short strokes precede canonique and another pair follows it. The word is legible; the substantive omission is the pair of quotation marks.

changes.place: Programme: raised g fixe and its comma
changes.ink: The small g fixe, lies above I variable and has a curved insertion leader after pour. The last e has no acute stroke above it, and the comma is part of the raised addition.

changes.place: Margin: short gén. and high double quotation marks
changes.ink: The first quoted word has g, an accented low vowel, n and a point, then a clear gap before et; there is no extra ér or ateurs run. Both quotation pairs are high double strokes, not angular guillemets.

changes.place: Margin: dash and following doubtful word
changes.ink: A short horizontal dash follows the closing quotes, then a d loop, accented low vowel and long f crossing the next line. The small ending is weak and near the right edge of the first crop; définies versus définis remains unresolved. H omits the entire dash-and-word group.
The last line starts a/l followed by the long descending g, then the é/b/r/i/q/u/e/s run. The initial al and middle b are incompatible with géométriques.
Immediately after pour is the compact two-t abbreviation, with its shared/crossing stroke; there is no independent cancellation stroke through a separate old word.

changes.place: Lower paragraph: H adds un before MD-graphe
changes.ink: The source moves directly from the compact tt to the capital M of MD-graphe; there is no intervening un. H's un does not correspond to additional ink.
After the initial descending g, the low run has the r/i sequence and dotted i before sation, without the extra al and tall l required by généralisation.

changes.place: Lower paragraph: position of the parenthesis
changes.ink: The whole parenthetic phrase stands at the beginning of the next physical line, before the cancelled donné and G→G′; H moves it after de MD-graphes. Spacing commands alone are not counted.

The struck word begins with the tall d, has lower rounded/arched remnants, and retains the final acute mark. The horizontal strike conceals the middle letters, so donné is a provisional reading rather than an unqualified restoration.
A separate dark descending comma follows the final s at the far right, outside all cancellation.

Déterminer is written above the struck définir. Its live letters are separate from the cancellation, while the old word's terminal bodies overlap the strike/replacement and retain local doubt. H has the replacement as ordinary following text.
The looped l/e article has no final s and the noun ends in the low e stroke before de; there is no terminal s on morphisme. Both endings are read from the ink.
This second occurrence again has the compressed génér-i-sation sequence, including the i dot, without an intervening al or tall l.
The word finishes with the tall angled t stroke; no separate final s follows before the displayed map.

A single dark, slightly right-drifting vertical stroke starts beside pour I variable and continues down beside the lower text, ending just above the bottom map. It is reproduced as a drawing; no verbal content is inferred.
Three pale lower-left figures are 1, closed 0 and double-curved 3. Their colour and position differ from the dark authorial 51 at the head; their hand is not identified.

doubts.reason: The compact low initial run does not separate the two o bodies of mono; the raised tick before p can instead be an i dot. Only the prefix is uncertain. This is added uncertainty against C, not a proved correction.
The old word is crossed through within the small raised insertion; several middle letter bodies cannot be independently recovered.
The dense horizontal stroke conceals much of the lower letter sequence; the provisional c/o/v beginning does not warrant removing C's doubt.

doubts.place: M1154: word after dash in diagonal margin
doubts.reason: The d/é/f beginning is visible but the small ending at the right edge of the first crop is not sufficiently separated. The blind box includes a wider region; no grammatical agreement is used to decide the e.
The initial d and final acute survive, but the strike conceals intervening bodies. Added uncertainty does not itself make C a substantive error.

alternatives: défi… with terminal letters partly obscured
doubts.reason: The initial défi is visible; terminal bodies are crowded by the cancellation and raised replacement. The whole-word doubt macro flags this local ending weakness, not uncertainty about every letter.

The horizontal shaft ends in a dense raised knot with a short downward spur; two independent branches of an ordinary arrowhead cannot be confidently separated. The objects, indices, prime and full stop are clear. This adds uncertainty to the shared witness arrow rather than proving a different symbol.

notes: The dark 51 at the head is retained as the authorial page number. The pale 103 at the lower left is separately retained as foliation without identifying its hand. Scan 104 is the digital sequence number, not an ink numeral.

The page continues a discussion of normalisation morphisms and their commutation with isomorphisms, writes the symmetric-group formula with I, I′ and I\I′, and then states a Programme concerning Π₁M_{g,I}, its normalisation maps, the extension SΠ₁M_G, and the corresponding generisation morphism. These are descriptions of what the page says, not verified mathematical results.
The written phrase les commutation is retained despite its article/noun mismatch. The raised g fixe has no acute on its final e; neither grammar nor H's fixé is used to add one.

The compact first prefix before ponctuels remains mono|uni after independent main-reader review. The visible raised tick can be an i dot, while the expected o bodies of mono are not separately exposed. The doubt is limited to the prefix.

The opening interlinear addition attaches between les and morphismes. Its old cancelled l'interaction is inside that addition and receives its own deletion record. The baseline pour pouvoir reconstituer is not an insertion, despite H's add wrapper.

After opening iso, the source shows only the separate comma; no distinct abbreviation point is visible. Both the first reader and main reader inspected the existing commutation crop before omitting C's extra point.
The underlined heading consists of the letters Programme, without an added following period. Both canonique and the marginal gén. et relations have high double quotation marks.

The diagonal note reads gén., not the expanded générateurs. M1154 remains définies|définis; its ending is not settled by agreement with relations or any inferred antecedent. The larger blind region includes the complete note and its surrounding Programme paragraph.

Both lower occurrences are générisation, retaining the written term instead of H's généralisation. The parenthesis (p.ex. un iso!) occurs before the cancelled donné and G→G′. The comma after MD-graphes remains live.

The product display has α as the first index of M and a hat on I_α. H's explanatory note about this index is editorial and is not transcribed as manuscript text. No g has been supplied. The lone Z has two diagonal strokes and is rendered as \mathbb Z; its exponent has a tilde over A.

The cancelled donné and définir receive added local uncertainty because the cancelling/replacement strokes obscure parts of their letter bodies. This certainty change is recorded in doubts and deletion checks, not counted as a substantive correction against C. The heavily retraced G before the ordinary G→G′ arrow does not establish a separate earlier deletion.

The final displayed map retains clear SΠ₁M_G and SΠ₁M_{G′}, with a final full stop. Only its compact endpoint is doubtful: ordinary full arrow versus downward harpoon. No proof or mathematical expectation is used to supply a missing arrowhead branch.
The long marginal stroke is reproduced as a TikZ drawing. Its slight drift and nonverbal nature are retained without deciding whether it was meant as a cancellation or a scope marker.

All current C/H word differences have inspected local crops. The original and both native halves were successfully viewed once each. Eleven local crops were created once and all were viewed; the existing opening and determine crops were re-opened at main-reader request, with no second crop or compilation. The main reader independently viewed the original and all eleven crops.

The line count is 29: 22 main written baselines, including three display rows, plus three interlinear rows and four diagonal marginal baselines. The two isolated page numerals and the nonverbal vertical rule are inventoried separately and excluded from the line count.

M1153 is resolved to C's first candidate gén. on the inspected crop. Following main-reader classification, that resolution alone is excluded from substantive C error counts; the same row remains a substantive H collation for its expanded word and quotation forms.
